title: Norris delighted to ‘give back’ to McLaren in Sao Paulo win
excerpt:
Lando Norris was thrilled to be able to give McLaren “a little bit of reward for their hard work” by winning the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, which marked his and the team’s third victory of the season.

Although the Briton started from pole position on the damp track, he quickly lost places to Kimi Antonelli and Liam Lawson, but recovered well to move up to second place and set his sights on the race lead.

As the surface dried out, Norris was amongst the first to switch from intermediate to slick tyres, giving him a clear advantage in terms of grip when he returned to challenge the Italian for first place.

A spin for Antonelli opened the door for him to sail back through, and he maintained the position amid more rain and another round of pit stops to cross the line over 14s ahead of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen.

“It was a very tough race – very, very tough,” Norris reflected. “Obviously, not the best of launches off the line, but a lot of challenges today, obviously, with the conditions.

“Going onto slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you're pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit.

“The main thing today was I just kept it cool and I didn't make any mistakes. I had the pace when I needed to, so it was good. Nice to be back on the top step, and what a place to do it as well.”

McLaren had slightly dropped away from the likes of Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull in recent rounds, but upgrades introduced at Interlagos seemed to provide the boost required to get back in the mix.

While Norris had looked strong throughout Free Practice, his skills in the wet made the difference in both Qualifying and the Grand Prix, leaving him grateful he was able to maximise every opportunity over the weekend.

Norris said: “We're trying, you know. I'm trying my best, and I think this weekend we had an opportunity to get pole yesterday, we had an opportunity to win.

“I feel like most times this year, when there's been an opportunity, I went for it and we've been able to achieve it. So I have to say a big thanks to the team because they're still working very hard.

“It's annoying when you can't give them a good result back, like the last few weeks. But certainly this weekend, I feel like we've been able to give something back to them and give them a little bit of reward for their hard work. So always a big thanks to them, and we have to keep pushing till the end of the year.”

title: Norris wins wet Sao Paulo GP thriller as Mercedes claim title
excerpt:
Lando Norris beat Max Verstappen to victory in a thrilling wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix as Mercedes clinched the 2026 Constructors' Championship.

Norris claimed his third win of the season during Sunday's 71-lap race at the Autódromo José Carlos Pace, which began wet and dried out before the McLaren driver had to navigate a late rain shower, eventually claiming victory by 14.6 seconds after starting from pole.

Verstappen climbed to the podium from P21 on the grid during a frenetic Grand Prix, as team mate Isack Hadjar made it a double podium for Red Bull.

George Russell and Kimi Antonelli finished fourth and fifth, the latter having spun twice – once even before the start – after leading early on, but with the result enough for Mercedes to claim the title.

Oscar Piastri (McLaren) was P6 ahead of Charles Leclerc, the Ferrari driver passing Liam Lawson on the penultimate lap after the Racing Bulls driver had run second in the opening laps.

Lewis Hamilton finished P9 on his 400th Formula 1 start, the Ferrari driver reaching the points after starting P20 and also suffering a spin, with the top 10 completed by Nico Hulkenberg's Audi.

Arvid Lindblad just missed out on the points for Racing Bulls but finished clear of Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso and the two Alpines of Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly.

Alex Albon was P15 for Williams, ahead of Brazilian home hero Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi), Ollie Bearman (Haas), Sergio Perez (Cadillac), Carlos Sainz (Williams), and Rafael Camara who finished P20 on his F1 debut for Haas.

Lance Stroll retired once again mid-race for Aston Martin, while Valtteri Bottas was wheeled off the grid before the start due to an issue with his Cadillac.

AS IT HAPPENED

There was drama even before the start of Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix, with new World Champion Antonelli running wide at Turn 12 on his reconnaissance lap as drivers assessed the damp but drying track, the Mercedes driver spinning his car and scrambling for grip on the wet grass.

The Italian eventually recovered back to the circuit and returned to the garage for precautionary checks with no lasting damage. If there were any lingering thoughts about the error, they were immediately dismissed once the red lights went out at the start as Antonelli jumped into the lead from second on the grid.

Having been beaten off the line, polesitter Norris eased his McLaren into Turn 1, allowing Lawson from the second row to move around the outside and giving the Racing Bulls driver the inside into Turn 2 and second place.

Further back, Hamilton was on an incredible charge, moving up from P20 on the grid to P9 before the end of the opening lap, while Verstappen moved up from P21 to P13.

Verstappen's charge continued and by Lap 5 the four-time World Champion had moved up to P8, demoting both Piastri and Albon in the space of two corners.

Hamilton, meanwhile, was placed under investigation for passing Bearman off track on the exit of Turn 5 on the opening lap, the Briton dropping to P11 and handing the position back to the Haas driver.

But the Ferrari driver was beginning to struggle with tyre wear, as the intermediate tyres began to quickly overheat and lose grip in the damp but quickly drying track.

Out in front, Lawson was also struggling with tyre wear, as Norris, Hadjar and Russell all moved ahead of the Kiwi in quick succession, with Verstappen soon overtaking as well having already cleared Hulkenberg.

By the end of Lap 14, Hamilton had dropped to P14 and became the first driver to pit for slick tyres, bolting on a set of soft Pirelli tyres, with Albon following in the next lap and prompting a flurry of pit lane action.

Norris, Russell and Hadjar pitted at the end of Lap 16, the McLaren driver having been 7s behind Antonelli, who along with Verstappen stayed out for an extra lap.

But Russell's race came undone in the pit lane exit, the Mercedes driver spinning backwards and losing crucial time and positions as he recovered, which included glancing the wall in his attempts to point the right way again.

Antonelli and Verstappen both pitted at the end of Lap 17, the former rejoining in the lead from Norris but by only a 2s margin, with Verstappen dropping back into P4 behind team mate Hadjar.

With warmer tyres Norris closed on Antonelli's out-lap, reducing the gap to just 0.6s across the line at the end of Lap 18, with Antonelli reporting "something is weird with the car", and suggesting a suspension issue.

Heading into Turn 1 at the start of Lap 20, Antonelli spun, giving Norris the lead as he rejoined just ahead of Hadjar, the Frenchman gaining P2 at the start of the next lap as Antonelli ran deep at Turn 1, with Verstappen the next to challenge.

Behind the leading quartet, Lawson was P5 from Piastri, with Hulkenberg heading the recovering Russell, Albon, Lindblad and Hamilton, who had made up ground after his early stop, with Alonso and Leclerc chasing.

By Lap 23 Overtake Mode was enabled, the track deemed completely dry as Norris held a 3.3s lead over Hadjar, with Antonelli off into the Turn 1 run-off again, rejoining once more but slipping back behind Verstappen.

The Dutchman was just 7s away from the race lead, as further back, Piastri moved ahead of Lawson for P5, Lindblad had moved into P9 as Albon dropped outside the points, with Leclerc also struggling and finding himself in P14.

Hamilton moved back ahead of Lindblad for P9 at Turn 1 on Lap 29, while up the road, Russell was struggling to find a way around Hulkenberg but finally secured the position into Turn 1 a lap later.

Drivers began to receive radio messages of potential rain in 10 laps, with Norris nearly 5s to the good over Hadjar, with Verstappen 8s away from the McLaren driver, as Antonelli had slipped to 15s adrift of the race lead.

The status quo remained for several laps, the closest battle for P11 as Albon defended from Alonso before the Williams driver ran wide at Turn 1 on Lap 35 and lost the position.

Albon regained the position through Turn 6 before Alonso swapped the positions at Turn 7, with Gasly holding a watching brief having had to back off when Albon rejoined at Turn 1, the Williams driver handed a five-second penalty for the incident.

Albon quickly lost further places to Gasly and Leclerc, while at the front, Hadjar suffered his own wide moment at Turn 1, eventually conceding P2 to team mate Verstappen into Turn 1 on Lap 38.

Norris' margin now stood at 9.2s, with Gasly and Hamilton taking on new sets of soft tyres as the expected rain shower appeared to be missing the circuit.

Hamilton was soon setting fastest laps but was stuck behind race leader Norris as the rest of the field remained out on their first set of slick tyres, Hamilton eventually unlapping himself on Lap 44.

In the battle for second, Hadjar remained within 1s of Verstappen and asked if the positions would be reversed, while Verstappen was being asked if he was able to run to the end on the same set of tyres before pitting at the end of Lap 45.

Verstappen rejoined P5 ahead of the recovering Russell, who had just overtaken Lawson into Turn 1, while Red Bull split their strategy as Hadjar confirmed he could run to the end but reporting light drops of rain.

Norris made his second stop at the end of Lap 49, rejoining back in P4, with Hadjar leading from Antonelli and Piastri as 21 laps remained.

Norris immediately passed Piastri on his out-lap, while Red Bull decided to pit Hadjar the next lap and he rejoined P6, behind Verstappen and Russell, but gained a position when Piastri pitted on Lap 51.

Both Hulkenberg and Lindblad moved ahead of Colapinto for the final point, but the former was handed a 10s penalty after going off the track at Turn 1, serving the punishment at a later stop.

Antonelli conceded the lead at the end of Lap 53 as he also headed to the pits, rejoining behind Russell and Hadjar as the pair battled into Turn 4, the Red Bull driver moving up to P3 as the threat of rain increased heading into the closing stages.

Russell moved aside for Antonelli at the start of Lap 57, as Lawson moved ahead of Leclerc for P7 at Turn 4, the Ferrari driver having stayed out on his first set of soft tyres as light rain began to fall.

Norris' margin stood at 10s, with Hadjar 7s further adrift and under pressure from Antonelli as lap times quickly began to increase with the track grip continuously dropping in the rain.

At the end of Lap 61, Russell and Alonso became the first drivers to stop for intermediate tyres as those who stayed out scrambled back round to the pits as everyone pitted for the appropriate tyre.

Hamilton spun on the climb up the hill from Turn 12, glancing the wall but recovering back to the pit lane, while Antonelli was placed under a post-race investigation after pulling into the path of an Alpine as he left his pit box.

Russell was soon on the tail of his team mate having been on his intermediates for an extra lap, Antonelli told to swap positions which he obeyed.

While Norris claimed his third win of the season and Red Bull claimed another double podium, Mercedes secured the title courtesy of Russell and Antonelli, with Piastri completing the top-six.

Leclerc made minor contact with Lawson in their battle for P7 at Turn 12, eventually sweeping around the outside of the Racing Bulls driver on the penultimate lap at Turn 3, with the top-10 completed by Hamilton and Hulkenberg.

Key quote

"It was a very tough race, very, very tough," said Norris. "Obviously, not the best of launches off the line, but a lot of challenges today, obviously with the conditions. Going onto slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you're pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit. So the main thing today was I just kept it cool and I didn't make any mistakes. And I had the pace when I needed to. So it was good. Nice to be back on the top step, and what a place to do it as well.

What's next

title: Hamilton's remarkable projects away from F1
excerpt:
This weekend’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix marks the 400th start for Lewis Hamilton in Formula 1. The seven-time World Champion has broken numerous records on track, including adding to his tally of 105 pole positions as recently as last weekend in Mexico, but is also one of racing's most influential personalities outside the paddock.

From his ventures in music and producing movies to being a co-chair during the 2025 Met Gala, Hamilton is a key figure in popular culture and has shown no signs of slowing down alongside his fast life in Formula 1. Here are some of the remarkable projects he has been involved with away from the track...

Rapping under a pseudonym

Hamilton has never shielded away from his love of creating music, even surprising fans with snippets of his songs during an Instagram Live broadcast in 2020. It received an excellent response, with several people begging for the champion to release a full album.

However, this wasn’t the first time we’d heard Hamilton on a track. Back in 2018, his friend Christina Aguilera released a song “Pipe” from her album Liberation featuring a mysterious guest artist, XNDA. Many had speculated that it sounded like Hamilton, but it was two years later when the driver of the #44 car confirmed his contribution to the track via an Instagram story.

“Guys, I've spent the last 10 years or more writing and recording, working with some of the most talented and beautiful people which I'm so grateful for,” Hamilton’s post said. “It's been the most incredible outlet. Finding something you love so much and can do just for you, for your spirit is I think such an important process.

"I've come to the place where I'd love to share it with you. I haven't got a project or album, just a bunch of different songs that perhaps some of you will be able to connect to. They have helped me get through some of the most difficult times. At some stage I'm going to find a moment to share with you so bare [sic] with me.

“I had this incredibly beautiful and talented person reach out to me a while back asking for me to be on her album. I was so blown away and I jumped at the opportunity. I had two hours to write the short verse and record.

"The goal was to have the music come out under a different name so that you could hear the music first and later know it was me but it didn't work out the way I'd planned. I shied away from acknowledging it was me, I don't know why, maybe insecurities, fear, overthinking, something I think many people can relate to.

“Well I want to say that XNDA is me and I am so honoured and grateful to Xtina for giving me a place to use my voice. I have so much gratitude and respect for her and what she's done in the business. #pipe”

Hamilton's incredible F1 records ahead of his 400th GP

Making appearances in video games

As well as the EA Sports F1 game, Hamilton can be found in several franchises: from Fortnite to Call of Duty.

The collaboration with Fortnite came in 2023, where users could play using their own playable skin of Hamilton. Sporting a colourful outfit and accompanied by his British bulldog Roscoe, who sadly passed away last year, Hamilton became a popular addition to the worldwide gaming phenomenon.

A decade ago, Hamilton also intercepted another gaming universe, with a cameo in the 2016 game Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. Posing as Carl Hamilton, a nod to Lewis’ middle name, the character is an electro-technical engineer and crew member.

He joined the cast for the game alongside F1 fan and Game of Thrones actor Kit Harington and Baywatch and Knight Rider legend David Hasselhoff, and had to have his face scanned for the role.

Playing his cards right

Hamilton has turned his childhood passion for collecting trading cards into his latest business venture, opening his very own store earlier this year.

The seven-time World Champion launched Card Culture by Lewis Hamilton, a trading card business created in partnership with Dave & Adam's Card World. The first flagship store opened in Frankfurt, Germany, in July, with plans to expand to other locations across Europe, Australia, the Middle East and Asia.

Hamilton's love of collecting stretches back to his childhood, when he would trade football cards with friends at school. His personal interests in the hobby have since expanded to include other sports and popular culture.

The Briton has also become something of a collector's item himself, with a rare, one-of-a-kind autographed Topps card featuring Hamilton selling for more than $1 million in December 2024, becoming the first Formula 1 trading card to reach a seven-figure sum.

“I remember being in school and the excitement of opening up packs of cards - growing up in England it was mostly football - and then trading them with friends,” Hamilton told Sports Illustrated.

“It was a small community, but we were connected through our love of sport and cards.”

For Hamilton, the venture is about more than simply selling collectibles. He hopes to create spaces where enthusiasts can share their passion, while introducing a new generation to the hobby.

“I look at it as building a modern card store that mixes community, culture, and competition,” he explained.

How Lewis Hamilton became F1's most influential fashion icon

A respected face in fashion

Throughout his Formula 1 career, Hamilton has become known for his distinctive sense of style, regularly experimenting with clothing, jewellery and accessories to express his personality. His paddock entrances have attracted attention well beyond the world of motorsport, while helping to encourage other drivers to embrace fashion as a form of self-expression.

The Briton has long been a familiar face at fashion shows, even making a cameo appearance as himself in the 2016 comedy sequel* Zoolander 2*, but in recent years his involvement in the industry has reached new heights.

One of his most significant fashion moments came in May 2025, when Hamilton was selected as one of five co-chairs of the prestigious Met Gala, joining Colman Domingo, A$AP Rocky, Pharrell Williams and Anna Wintour.

Held annually at New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Met Gala raises funds for the museum's Costume Institute and celebrates the opening of its annual fashion exhibition. The 2025 exhibition, titled Superfine: Tailoring Black Style, explored the history and cultural significance of Black dandyism and its influence on fashion and identity.

To mark the occasion, Hamilton also appeared on the cover of Vogue's May 2025 issue, with the magazine releasing four special covers celebrating the event's co-chairs. Photographed by Malick Bodian, Hamilton wore a Ferragamo suit and off-white bow tie for the cover, further cementing his status as one of the sport's most recognisable figures in fashion.

Hamilton, who made his Met Gala debut in 2015, has also established partnerships with several major fashion brands, serving as a Dior menswear ambassador and guest designer, as well as becoming lululemon's inaugural motorsport ambassador.

Making his way into the movies

Another creative outlet for the seven-time champion is Hollywood. He has previously shared that some of his favourite films are Coming to America, Interstellar and *Ferris Bueller’s Day Off *– with Hamilton recreating the latter on his own social media last year.

His role as a producer – and briefly a cast member – for F1: The Movie has also served as a great source of education and enthusiasm for Hamilton, who has been very vocal about his love for director Joseph Kosinski.

“Coming on board to this project as a producer has been such an incredible learning process for me, seeing what goes into making a feature film, and there’s been a lot of learning on the other side too as everyone has got to grips with Formula 1,” Hamilton explained last year.

“I’ve always loved film and telling stories, and I’ve loved this sport since I was five years old, so when I got the opportunity to speak with Joe Kosinski and Jerry Bruckheimer about the project, it felt like the two worlds I’m passionate about coming together.

“I remember in the early days of the project I got to meet with Brad [Pitt] and go through the script, join meetings with the teams at Apple and Formula 1, and be part of some of the early casting processes. From those first conversations, to watching it all come together, it’s just been a super cool experience and I can’t wait for everyone to see it!”

Kosinski – who also directed Top Gun: Maverick – was apparently approached by Hamilton to appear in the showstopping fighter jet film. As a fan of the original like most of us, and his close friendship with Tom Cruise, it was believed that Hamilton asked them both for a part in the film when it was confirmed that a sequel was in the works.

Joking that he’d even be a “cleaner in the back and sweep something”, Hamilton was then given the green light and told he could be a pilot in the movie. Unfortunately for us F1 fans, Lewis described the “most upsetting call that I think I've ever had” in a GQ interview, where he had to turn down the opportunity due to clashes with the Formula 1 calendar.

title: Liam Lawson casts doubt over 'legality' of race-defining Charles Leclerc overtake
excerpt:
Liam Lawson has cast doubt over the legality of Charles Leclerc's late overtake on him for seventh place in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

On lap 69 of 71 in the wet conditions, Leclerc biffed Lawson out of the way at Turn 12 to climb the hill, with the right-front tyre making contact with Lawson's left-rear, forcing the New Zealander wide.

This then gave Leclerc better momentum up the hill, and although Lawson stayed ahead into Turn 1, the Ferrari driver got ahead for seventh place on the road into Turn 4 on the next lap after a thrilling wheel-to-wheel battle.

Lawson finished eighth, but could capitalise if Leclerc is handed any penalty, as he was 1.816s behind over the line.

Leclerc has been called to the stewards regarding the incident for allegedly causing a collision, with Lawson saying the move reminded him of Leclerc's move on Alex Albon in the 2017 GP2 race at Abu Dhabi - where Leclerc did a 'bump and run' on Albon into the hairpin before the long back straight, using this momentum to get ahead for the win.

Reflecting, Lawson branded the move as Leclerc's "specialty."

"I think it was his wing which hit my tyre, so I think we got really lucky," Lawson said of Leclerc's move to media, including RacingNews365.

"I feel like it was exactly like his GP2 move on Albon in Abu Dhabi years ago; he did the same kind of thing, so maybe it is his speciality.

"I don't know if it is legal or not, and we'll go and review it, but it was a good battle overall."

[Article continues below]

Potential Antonelli attack

Fast-starting from third, Lawson initially felt he could have attacked leader Kimi Antonelli and taken the lead of a grand prix for the first time.

"It was a crazy race, honestly, I had a really good start, good grip into Turn 1 and made a place up and was thinking I might try and attack Kimi at some point in the lap," he said.

"But once the pace stabilised, they're a lot quicker than us, and we started to fall back, we were damaging the tyre quite a lot more than them, and then the pace in the dry was okay.

"At the end, I tried to keep Charles before, we had some contact into Turn 12 , ended up losing the place."

title: Lewis Hamilton reveals 'ballooned' moment that played havoc in Sao Paulo
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has revealed that the rear tyres on his first stint in his Ferrari "ballooned and overheated" during a chaotic São Paulo Grand Prix

From the 20th on the Interlagos grid following a multitude of power unit penalties, Hamilton started brilliantly, rising to ninth by the end of the first lap.

But from there, his race slowly unravelled, initially on the opening set of intermediates in the wet conditions before making a superb early call to switch to the soft slicks.

Running on a second set of soft Pirellis late in the race, Hamilton spun up the hill as he was preparing to return to the pits for a new set of inters, kissing a barrier with the rear wing of his SF-26 as he tried to control the slide.

The seven-time F1 champion ultimately finished ninth and a lap down on race winner Lando Norris in his McLaren.

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 after the race, Hamilton explained how the handling problems hit almost immediately once the lights went out.

"A really tough day and weekend for the whole team, but they've done a really great job, switching out the engine, making sure the car was as strong as it could be," said Hamilton.

"We struggled in the dry, but I had a great start. Unfortunately, the rear tyres just ballooned and overheated, and I then struggled.

"After that, I was pushing to go to the slicks, which I eventually got on. I was one of the earlier ones, and was feeling pretty good. It was very tricky in those conditions.

"And then we ended up having an extra stop, and I had a lot of ground to cover from there.

"At the end, the last message I got was that it was going to stay drizzling, and I was like, 'Okay, this is my moment to keep pushing', and I could stay in those conditions.

"I didn't hear that it was raining more in the first sector, and I passed the pit lane, got to Turn 1 and it was wet, so that unfortunately lost us a couple of places, otherwise, the team did a great job."

With three rounds remaining in the season, Hamilton admitted he was unsure what to expect from Ferrari's pace heading into the final stretch.

"I really don't know where we're going to be in the next races, but we've had a really good car in the past races," he said. "This weekend was a bit of a struggle.

"I think that the team deserved a better result. But we live and we learn, and we will come back and try and fight harder at the next one."

title: Kimi Antonelli among F1 drivers summoned to stewards after Sao Paulo GP
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli has been summoned to the F1 stewards following the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Elsewhere, Charles Leclerc has been called for the penultimate-lap incident with Liam Lawson, where he barged the Racing Bulls' out of the way at Juncao to climb the hill - and was able to get ahead.

Leclerc has been called to answer for allegedly causing a collision with the New Zealander, with Leclerc going on to finish in seventh with Lawson close behind in eighth.

Finally, Oliver Bearman has also been called for an alleged unsafe release in the pit-lane.

Leclerc will be seen by the stewards at 16:45 local time, and Bearman at 17:15 local time.

title: Toto Wolff responds to matching F1 icon feat: 'Never thought it possible'
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has conceded that he "never thought it possible" he would match the feat of F1 icon Sir Frank Williams.

For the ninth time, Mercedes are constructors' champions, overseen by team principal Wolff, who has now drawn level with Williams for third on the all-time list.

The title was confirmed after a messy race in Brazil, where Lando Norris took victory for McLaren ahead of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, with George Russell and Kimi Antonelli salvaging fourth and fifth for Mercedes despite a difficult afternoon.

Russell had started seventh after a five-place grid penalty, whilst he also spun in the pit lane exit at one stage after a wet-to-dry tyre change.

Antonelli also spun twice, once before the start and again at Turn 1 while running at the front, as he struggled to get temperature into his tyres.

It was Mercedes' first race of the season without a podium finish, but it did not matter: the result was enough to put the title beyond Ferrari's reach with three rounds still to run.

Asked about matching Williams's tally, speaking to Sky Sports F1, Wolff said:

"Obviously, Frank is such an unbelievable icon of the sport, and to be tied on constructors' championships, I never thought that was ever possible," he said.

"I had a close relationship with Frank, and to be there, it's amazing. I can't believe it.

"But also, fair justice. There are some of our people who have won more than mine, who were with Brawn, winning it with Honda, God knows what, and they have more. So yeah, I take it. It's great."

Reflecting on the shape of the campaign overall that has yielded the first constructors' title after its run of eight from 2014 to 2021, Wolff added: "It's amazing.

"It was a very strong beginning of the season, and that got us over the line. These last few races, there have been some challenging times.

"Today, it was difficult, but overall, I'm so proud of the organisation.

"We've taken a few years to be back in the top spot. Not many teams have been able to come back from such a situation, and it just shows the great work, the great people that we have in our organisation, and it's fantastic to be among them."

title: Lando Norris suffers another podium disaster after smashing Sao Paulo celebrations
excerpt:
Lando Norris suffered another podium disaster in his smashing celebrations at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Norris claimed his third victory of the season in Interlagos in a wet and wild race, beating Max Verstappen by 14.6s and Isack Hadjar by 24.4 to record his 14th career victory, and first since the Netherlands in August.

However, after the British national anthem and receiving his trophy, Norris went to conduct his usual podium celebration of smashing the champagne bottle to spray it - but unfortunately, he did so too hard and smashed the bottle to the ground.

He then took a few moments to compose himself after the smash - which is the second podium incident he's had.

After the 2023 Hungarian GP, when he smashed the champagne bottle, he accidentally did so too close to Verstappen's winner's trophy, knocking it off the top step and smashing it.

title: Max Verstappen bemoans 'completely opposite' feeling despite Sao Paulo stunner
excerpt:
Max Verstappen described a "completely different" and "weird" feeling with his Red Bull during another superlative performance in the São Paulo Grand Prix.

For the third consecutive year, Verstappen started from a position that suggested a podium was highly improbable, yet for the third consecutive season, the four-time F1 champion managed to finish in the top three, claiming the runner-up spot on this occasion after starting 21st

Two years ago, Verstappen won from 17th on the grid; last season, he was third from the pit lane.

Assessing his latest heroics in a wet-dry-wet race, the Red Bull driver, speaking to Sky Sports F1, said: "It was a challenging race.

"I think the first few laps, of course, were very important. I overtook a lot of cars, and actually, that first stint, I think, on the inter was really, really strong."

Verstappen made most of his headway on the first set of inters before a switch so softs prevented further major progress.

"Unfortunately, after that, I don't know if we picked up some kind of damage because the car felt completely opposite to anything that I felt the whole weekend, with some really weird balance," he said.

"Unfortunately, once I got into P2, I couldn't really make any inroads. So we have to understand what went wrong there."

After another inter spell late in the race as the rain fell again, Verstappen finished 14 seconds behind race winner Lando Norris.

He at least acknowledged his performance, however, adding: "I mean, starting P 21 and being on the podium in second is a very good result."

title: Max Verstappen repeats Sao Paulo heroics as Lando Norris seals victory
excerpt:
Another belter of a race at Interlagos as the drivers survived the wet-dry-wet conditions.

8 November 7:44PM

Lando Norris scored his third victory of the season, and his second successive win in São Paulo on a day when Mercedes netted the F1 constructors' championship.

In a highly entertaining wet-dry-wet race around Interlagos, Norris finished 14.6 seconds ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who delivered another stunning drive in Brazil after starting 21st.

Two years ago, the four-time F1 champion won from 17th on the grid; last year, he was third after starting from the pit lane.

Verstappen was joined on the podium by Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar, his third top-three finish for the team in his first season with the Milton Keynes-based squad.

Mercedes duo George Russell and incoming champion Kimi Antonelli were fourth and fifth to secure Mercedes its team title. The 20-year-old is under investigation for an unsafe release, although with McLaren's Oscar Piastri 20 seconds adrift in sixth, even a 10-second penalty will not hurt that position.

[Article continues below]

Max Verstappen repeats Sao Paulo heroics as Lando Norris seals victory

# Driver Team Time Tyre

Results are being loaded...

Verstappen surges forward

At the start, on a wet track with all the drivers on intermediates, Antonelli managed to get a flyer and leave pole sitter Norris in his wake.

Norris' struggle continued through the Senna S as Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson made his way past into second, a position he finally regained on lap seven. A lap later, the New Zealander was down to fifth after also being passed by Hadjar and Mercedes' George Russell.

By that stage, from 21st on the grid, Verstappen had risen to sixth, whilst Hamilton, who made up 11 places from 20th to ninth on the opening lap, was running in 11th.

One of those positions was to Verstappen, who made a sweeping move up the hill at one stage, whilst the seven-time F1 champion also had to give a place back to Haas' Oliver Bearman after going off track and gaining an advantage with a move on lap one.

By the end of lap 11, and clearly struggling with his rear tyres, Hamilton had dropped to 14th after being overtaken by Racing Bull's Arvid Lindblad, his Scuderia team-mate Charles Leclerc, and even Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso.

Hamilton and Leclerc went wheel to wheel along the main straight but after recent issues between the duo, and clear-the-air talks on Thursday evening in São Paulo, they managed to stay out of each other's way on this occasion.

At the end of lap 15, Hamilton was the first to make the switch to slicks, taking on a set of softs and dropping back to the position he started from - 20th - with the Briton followed into the pits by Williams' Carlos Sainz, who also took on softs.

The duo sparked a welter of stops, including Russell, who spun in the middle of the pit lane exit and at one point was facing the wrong way. From fourth on track at the stop, he lost four places by the time he managed to extricate himself from an awkward position.

After 19 laps, all drivers had completed a stop. At the start of lap 20, Antonelli spun out of the lead at Turn 1, allowing Norris to sweep by. A lap later, and seemingly struggling with a car pulling to one side under acceleration, Antonelli was passed by Hadjar.

[Article continues below]

The rain strikes again

Antonelli's woes continued on lap 24 as Verstappen moved up into the podium places, seven seconds behind leader Norris, and with team-mate Hadjar in between the pair.

A frantic radio message to engineer Pete Bonnington underlined the issue he was experiencing, in that he could not "turn left on the corners", and that "the car was turning by itself".

Approaching the midway point of the race, and with Norris holding a 7.5s lead over Hadjar, with Verstappen closing in, Lance Stroll suffered his 14th retirement of a miserable season in his Aston Martin, now two shy of the record held by Andrea de Cesaris.

On lap 37, Red Bull called for Hadjar to pull to one side and allow Verstappen to pass into second, which he obliged by doing so into Turn 1 on the following lap.

At the end of lap 39, Hamilton, in ninth, was the first to take on fresh rubber for a second time, again taking on softs, falling to 14th. As he emerged out of the pits, he found himself passed by Norris to fall a lap down.

Hamilton managed to unlap himself at the start of lap 44, at which point Norris was holding a 10.5s lead over Verstappen, who had not managed to pull away from Hadjar. The French-Algerian driver continued to remain within a second of his team-mate.

After 46 laps, Verstappen also opted for new Pirellis. In contrast, Hadjar was asked whether he wanted to go to the end on his first set of softs, making it clear he would do so.

With 24 laps remaining, Verstappen found himself in fifth, 35 seconds behind Norris, with Hadjar, Antonelli and McLaren's Oscar Piastri also in front of him.

Norris, though, pitted after 49 laps, handing the lead to Hadjar, with the Briton dropping to fourth behind Piastri, who quickly moved aside to allow him through to third.

Despite his earlier claim, Hadjar did pit again a lap later, promoting Antonelli back into the lead, although he, too, boxed after 54 laps, giving Norris a 7.5s advantage over Verstappen in the battle for the victory.

It was then that light rain started to fall, but Norris was able to stretch his lead over Verstappen to 14 seconds after 62 laps before pitting for inters, whilst Verstappen stayed out for one more lap, as did seventh-placed Hamilton, who lost his Ferrari up the hill, almost losing his car into a barrier, kissing it with his rear wing.

With all the drivers back on inters, Antonelli was told to let Russell by into fourth in the hope he could chase down Hadjar for third, but it was to no avail.

Norris managed the wet conditions through to the flag to clinch his first win since the Dutch GP at Zandvoort at the end of August.

Behind the top five, Leclerc, Lawson, Hamilton and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg completed the top 10.

title: Breaking: Mercedes end painful five-year wait by reclaiming F1 constructors’ title
excerpt:
Mercedes has won the F1 constructors' title for the ninth time after a wild Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Heading into the race, the team had 630 points compared to Ferrari on 504, a gap of 126, with 172 points left on the board, and the team knew it required a 129-point buffer after the race to be assured of its title.

It meant Kimi Antonelli from second and George Russell from seventh on the grid, were required to out-score Ferrari by just three points to be assured of the title.

Russell finished fourth and Antonelli fifth for a haul of 22 points, with Charles Leclerc in seventh and Lewis Hamilton in ninth for Ferrari, for eight points. It means Mercedes' lead is 140 points, with 129 left in the final three races.

It is Mercedes' first constructors' title since 2021, when its record-breaking run of eight consecutive titles ended in the first year of the ground-effect rules, when the team badly got its car design wrong - with the next four titles since Mercedes' last split between Red Bull and McLaren.

Mercedes has now moved level with Williams in third for the most F1 constructors' titles.

title: Lance Stroll closing in on all-time F1 record after latest Aston Martin failure
excerpt:
Lance Stroll suffered yet another retirement in the 2026 season, with his 13th DNF in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

title: Lando Norris pinpoints 'main' factor behind dominant Sao Paulo F1 victory
excerpt:
Lando Norris has pinpointed his ability to "keep it cool" and not make "mistakes" as the key reasons behind his return to winning ways at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix for McLaren.

From pole position, Norris was jumped off the line by Kimi Antonelli and followed the Mercedes throughout the intermediate tyre stint until the crossover.

Norris pitted one lap prior to Antonelli and was able to use his hotter tyres to eat into the lead of the Mercedes driver and mount an attack into Turn 1.

Antonelli then spun, allowing Norris through for a lead he would not yield.

Norris then survived the second stop to another set of soft tyres, and then the late rain shower and change to intermediate rubber, as he won his 14th grand prix and third of the season by 14.602s from Max Verstappen.

"It was a very tough race, very very tough," Norris reflected.

"Obviously, it was not the best of launches off the line, but there were a lot of challenges with the conditions and going on slicks in the wet is always tough, especially when you're pushing for the lead and trying to catch up a little bit.

"So, the main thing today was that I kept it cool, didn't make any mistakes, and had the pace when I needed to. So, it was good.

"It is nice to be back on the top step."

[Article continues below]

Return to winning ways

After the third win of the season following McLaren's recent lean spell, Norris spoke of taking his chances when it was possible.

"This weekend we had an opportunity to get a pole, and we had an opportunity to win, and I feel like most times this year, when it's been an opportunity, I went for it, and we've been able to achieve it," he said.

"So I have to say a big thanks to the team because they're still working very hard, and it's annoying when you can't give them a good result back like in the last few weeks.

"But certainly this weekend, I feel like we've been able to give something back to them and give them a little bit of reward for their hard work. So, always a big thanks to them, and we have to keep pushing till the end of the year."

title: George Russell spin nearly blocks pit-lane after crucial Sao Paulo pit-stop
excerpt:
George Russell nearly blocked the Sao Paulo Grand Prix pit-lane after spinning following a crucial pit-stop.

With the field starting on the intermediate tyres in the damp conditions at Interlagos, the track started to dry quickly, with the fast-starting but quickly dropping-down-the-order Lewis Hamilton eager to stop for dry tyres.

Hamilton and Carlos Sainz triggered the charge for red-marked soft tyres on Lap 15, with the field coming in at the end of the next lap, with second-placed Lando Norris, third-placed Russell, fourth-placed Isack Hadjar and fifth-placed Liam Lawson all following suit.

However, when exiting the pits on his soft tyres, Russell spun and lost control and was forced to drive the wrong way briefly to turn around, as the likes of Hadjar, Lawson, and Oscar Piastri filtered through.

It meant Russell fell to eighth once the order had shaken out.

Team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who was leading the race, did not stop until next time by, but his hard-earned lead over Norris was eradicated, with the McLaren immediately on the back of the Mercedes, who then spun from the lead at Turn 1, as he reported a potential issue.

title: How Mercedes can win 2026 F1 constructors' title in Sao Paulo Grand Prix
excerpt:
With the drivers' title in the bag for Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes head to the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on the cusp of winning the constructors' title for another championship double.

As it stands, Mercedes has 630 points to nearest challenger Ferrari on 504 - a gap of 126 points heading into the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

With four rounds still planned, it means there are 172 points left on the table - with 129 remaining following the race weekend at Interlagos.

It means that for Mercedes to claim the 2026 F1 constructors' title in Brazil, it must simply outscore Ferrari by three points or more.

Antonelli starts from second place on the grid, with George Russell in seventh after his engine penalty.

For Ferrari, Charles Leclerc is 14th after his penalty, and Lewis Hamilton is 20th after one of his own.

These positions would be good enough for Mercedes to clinch the title.

At the very least, if Ferrari fail to score in Sao Paulo, Antonelli or Russell would be required to finish at least eighth - and earn four points.

For Ferrari to continue the fight to Las Vegas, it must out-score Mercedes by four or more points, meaning an eighth-place finish is the minimum required if Mercedes fail to score.

If the gap is exactly 126 points following the Sao Paulo GP, Mercedes will win on countback, with the team enjoying 12 wins to Ferrari's two at present, with the number of wins used as the first tie-breaker when points are level.

Should Mercedes win the constructors' title in 2026, it will be the team's ninth title overall - drawing level with Williams for third on the all-time list.

title: Max Verstappen handed sensational Sao Paulo Grand Prix verdict
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has emerged as the clear favourite among RacingNews365 readers to win the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, with 32.6 per cent backing the Red Bull to perform a sensational recovery.

Verstappen's support comes despite Red Bull fitting a fresh internal combustion engine, turbocharger and exhaust on his car for the weekend, forcing him to start at the back of the grid, as is Hamilton.

The Dutchman has also flagged that this year's energy deployment regulations make overtaking down the Interlagos main straight tougher than in previous seasons, with smaller closing speeds between cars.

Even so, readers appear to be banking on history repeating itself. Interlagos has long been a happy hunting ground for Verstappen, whose most famous win there came in 2024, when he recovered from seventeenth on the grid to triumph in treacherous conditions.

The circuit's reputation for shifting grip levels, rain and safety cars has repeatedly rewarded strong car control and bold strategy calls, qualities that have defined the four-time champion's drives there in the past.

title: George Russell issues F1 'horrific accident' warning after survival challenge
excerpt:
George Russell has warned that the conditions in qualifying for the São Paulo Grand Prix could have produced a "horrific" crash had the conditions seen during the session actually occurred during the race itself.

The Mercedes driver finished second behind Lando Norris in a qualifying session at Interlagos that was thrown into chaos by a torrential downpour, with the opening segment red-flagged after just two minutes due to standing water and zero visibility.

Drivers immediately reported aquaplaning even on the full wet tyres, forcing race control to send out the medical and safety cars to inspect the circuit before suspending the session for 82 minutes.

Russell described the early laps of Q1 as some of the most difficult he has faced, saying the spray made it impossible to see the braking zone for Turn 4.

"Yeah, I mean, especially Q1 was extremely challenging," said Russell. "You know, the visibility was zero down the straight into Turn 4. I was wheel-spinning in fifth gear, over 200 kilometres an hour, aquaplaning.

"So, when you're aquaplaning on the straight and you can't see in front of you, it's... I'm not even sure what the word is to describe it. You know, it does seem a bit crazy, I guess that's what we have to deal with.

"I love driving in the rain. I love driving in the rain here, but at some point, if that was a race, there was no way we should be driving in that because the chances of seeing a really, really horrific incident are very, very high."

How Russell kept busy during lengthy qualifying stoppage

With qualifying halted for well over an hour, Russell found an unusual way to pass the time in the Mercedes garage.

Asked how he passed the time during the stoppage, Russell replied: "Played some chess. That was about it, really.

"Spoke with the mechanics, and I was pretty convinced it was not going to restart. But I think, yeah, nice that we did."
